bullets.title: NVDA: Multiple headwinds — export controls, CEO scandal, BofA US1 removal, PT cuts
bullets.body: NVDA faces a perfect storm: FBI probe into Jensen Huang's alleged relationship with a Chinese-linked executive enabling $7.5B+ chip shipments, White House considering new advanced chip export controls, general counsel allegedly intervening in Commerce Dept probe, and class action lawsuit. BofA removed NVDA from US 1 List (maintains Buy). Citi trimmed PT to $285 (from prior) on 19x P/E; Mizuho cut to $250 from $315; JPM flagged governance/succession risk (60% direct reports). Stock shed ~$200B market cap/-4.5% close; AMD +13% and semicap +6.85% as competitors seize opportunity. Jan-Q guide implies $125B (+15% QoQ) on Rubin ramp; FY28 ~70% growth thesis intact but CEO overhang is now a structural discount factor.

bullets.title: NVDA/MU/AVGO: BofA removes trio from US 1 List; maintains Buy on all three
bullets.body: BofA removed Lam Research, Micron, and NVDA from its US 1 List while keeping Buy ratings on all three. Separately, NVDA/MU/AVGO collectively account for ~45% of projected 2027 SPX EPS growth per UBS, which maintains a bullish sector view.

bullets.title: TTD: Q3 massive beat/raise but stock -5% pre-mkt on structural concerns; UBS upgrades to Buy
bullets.body: TTD Q3 revenue $736M vs. consensus $651M; adj. EBITDA $266M vs. $162M; Q4 guided $755M+ revenue and $280M+ EBITDA vs. Street $688M/$192M. However, 12% buy/67% hold/21% sell sell-side skew reflects concerns about ~$3ppt one-time Q3 tailwind, political spend fade (~25% decline Q4-Q1), AI/walled-garden competition, and core growth deceleration ex-items. UBS upgraded to Buy, PT $19 (from $15), raising FY27/28 EBITDA 24%/35%; DA Davidson assumed Neutral at $15 PT. TTD also approved $731M additional buyback.

bullets.title: TTWO: GTA VI pre-orders 'unprecedented'; Street bullish into Nov 19 launch despite mixed Q2
bullets.body: TTWO Q2 adj. EPS $0.99 beat vs. $0.96; net bookings $1.60B light vs. $1.62B on NBA 2K weakness. FY27 net bookings guidance reaffirmed $8.0-8.2B (+19-22%), embedding ~34M GTA VI unit sales. Wolfe reiterates Outperform at $289 PT (39% upside); UBS Buy at $295; ROTH Buy at $272. GTA Online recurrent spend could add $2.6-3.3B in FY28-29 bookings. Street broadly views recent underperformance (-19% YTD) as the buying opportunity into the decade's most important release.

bullets.title: CSCO: JPM reiterates OW/$150 PT; expects beat-and-raise on AI networking demand
bullets.body: JPM forecasts F1Q27 revenue $18.4B vs. $18.1B guidance midpoint; EPS $1.35 vs. $1.33 guide. Raises FY27 AI revenue target to ~$8.5B (+100%+ growth) and expects FY27 revenue guidance to lift to +16-17%. Stock down 17% from October peak to ~$98.65, bringing NTM P/E to 18-19x — JPM calls this a 'more palatable setup.' Networking segment expected +40% y/y in F1Q27.

bullets.title: AVGO: Confirmed as Google TPU supplier through 2028+; no revenue growth slowdown expected
bullets.body: JPM confirms AVGO is the unchallenged supplier for Google's v8i Max TPU (2x compute, 2H27 ramp) and v9.5/v10 2nm SKU (mid-2028 production). No TPU revenue growth slowdown expected through CY31. Google's $26B Anthropic cornerstone investment and TPU roadmap alignment reinforce AVGO's AI ASIC moat.

bullets.title: MSFT: Azure at 48% CC growth; lobbying to block Chinese optical transceiver ban; IBM partnership
bullets.body: RBC flags Azure acceleration at 48% constant currency; Ignite conference expected to showcase full-stack AI integration. MSFT is lobbying the White House to halt a planned ban on Chinese optical transceivers, arguing it would slow data center buildout (35 centers under construction, 134 more planned). IBM and MSFT also launched 'Imagine Enterprise,' an agentic AI platform for industry-specific transformation.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO (ANT): $61B deal priced $70-78/sh; $26B cornerstone from NVDA, MSFT, GOOGL, AVGO, MU, AMD, TSM
bullets.body: Anthropic files amended S-1 for 825M Class A shares at $70-78/sh (~$61B raise); concurrent $26B private placement from AMD, AVGO, GOOGL, MU, MSFT, NVDA, and TSMC at IPO price. Roadshow Nov 10-18, pricing post-close Nov 18, trading Nov 19. Valuation has declined from earlier $1.5-2T expectations to ~$1T at top of range. Proceeds earmarked for compute infrastructure and hiring.

bullets.title: TSM: October sales +59.7% YoY to $17.9B; Q4 guided +15% QoQ on N3/N2 AI ramp
bullets.body: TSMC reported October monthly revenue NT$586.6B (+59.7% YoY), tracking toward record Q4 on N3 AI accelerator/CPU demand and N2 ramp. Q4 revenue guided $52.3-54.3B; analyst consensus implies ~63% YoY growth. TSMC also approved $40.9B capex budget for 2027.

bullets.title: U (Unity): Take-private buzz at ~$25B ($49.60/sh); 25% q/q DAU growth strengthens bull case
bullets.body: MS reports a consortium including Silver Lake (owns ~8% of U) and Saudi PIF discussed a ~$25B take-private at $49.60/share; both investors participated in EA's $55B take-private. Bull case implies $95 valuation with 80% incremental EBITDA margins from Vector growth. Separately, Jefferies notes 25% q/q DAU growth with positive downstream monetization impacts.

bullets.title: CRWV: Highest financing risk in coverage (4.5/5); $38.6B requirement through 2027
bullets.body: OPCO assigns CRWV the highest financing risk score (4.5/5) among 12 companies, estimating $38.6B in capital requirements through 2027 — exceeding current market cap. Existing cash/OCF covers only ~40% of planned capex in a 30% downside scenario, though signed customer contracts provide spend flexibility. UBS notes CRWV is down >40% since Q2; FQ3 expectations: $3.54B revenue, ($1.27) EPS, with management guiding low-teens op margins in Q4.

bullets.title: INTC: Management bullish on 2027 — server CPU +30%, purpose-built silicon +100% YoY
bullets.body: RBC and JPM both flag INTC management confidence: server CPU units tracking 30%+ growth in 2027, purpose-built silicon growing 100% y/y (lower margin mix), Israel fab restart on track, foundry advanced packaging wins expected to ramp 2H27. Both firms maintain Sector Perform/Neutral due to premium valuation and limited near-term catalysts despite constructive 2027 framework.

bullets.title: NET: DZ Bank upgrades to Buy from Sell; PT $300
bullets.body: DZ Bank reversed its Sell rating on Cloudflare, upgrading to Buy with a $300 PT (from $275), implying ~2% upside from current $293.75. FactSet consensus PT is $347 with range $190-430, suggesting DZ remains below consensus even at Buy.

bullets.title: MDB: BTIG initiates Buy at $417 PT (27% upside)
bullets.body: BTIG analyst Gray Powell initiated MongoDB at Buy with a $417 price target vs. current $327.37, implying 27% upside. FactSet consensus target is $458.82 (range $372-565), so BTIG's target is below the Street average but directionally aligned.

bullets.title: STX: Down 43% in 3 months while EPS estimates rose 25-50%; trading 5.2x CY28 EPS
bullets.body: MS flags STX as deeply undervalued: stock down 43% over three months while EPS estimates rose 25-50%; now trading 5.2x CY28 EPS vs. historical trough multiples. AI HDD demand is accelerating beyond supply, with pricing accelerating and improving incremental margins. STX can buyback ~30% of the company over 2-2.5 years on growing FCF.

bullets.title: HIMS: JPM cuts PT to $24 from $32; marketing pause weighs near-term, 2027 reacceleration thesis intact
bullets.body: JPM maintains Neutral on HIMS, cutting PT to $24 from $32. 3Q revenue $890M (+49% YoY) in-line but subscribers declined ~100K QoQ from domestic weight-loss marketing pause; gross margin compressed 700bps QoQ to ~57%. International revenue grew 321% to $233M (including Eucalyptus). JPM projects 2027 revenue $3.71B (+19%) with 9.6% adj. EBITDA margins. Key risks: GLP-1 margin compression, Eli Lilly/Amazon competition, potential Novo partnership termination.

bullets.title: AAON: Beat-and-raise with record data center orders; PT raised to $105; FCF inflects positive
bullets.body: AAON beat with margin outperformance despite HVAC sector headwinds; record quarterly data center orders expected in Q4; FCF inflected positive for first time in two years. PT raised to $105 with the analyst arguing current price values the data center business at zero. Declining capex y/y provides buyback firepower into FY27.

bullets.title: ADBE: Disney multi-year alliance validates Firefly Foundry enterprise monetization
bullets.body: RBC flags ADBE's multi-year Disney alliance as validation of its Firefly Foundry GenAI enterprise strategy, with cost savings and productivity the core TAM driver. This is viewed as a meaningful enterprise monetization proof point for ADBE's AI product suite.

bullets.title: META: Building enterprise AI salesforce; Muse Ember model competitive with Claude/GPT; VR partnership with Pixelworks
bullets.body: JPM flags META hiring enterprise sales team and consulting partners for AI products following $145B capex commitment. META Muse Ember delivers more intelligence-per-dollar than Claude Haiku or GPT-6 Luna; models now available on Google Cloud. Separately, Pixelworks announced multi-year TrueCut Motion certification partnership with Meta VR Glasses.

bullets.title: CSCO/NVDA earnings previews; NVDA Jan-Q at $125B, CSCO F1Q27 beat expected Thu Nov 12
bullets.body: Key upcoming prints: NVDA reports Tue Nov 17 after close ($2.47 EPS/$108.8B revenue consensus; Citi models $109B revenue, $125B Jan-Q on Rubin ramp). CSCO reports Thu Nov 12 after close ($1.32 EPS/$18.11B consensus; JPM models $18.4B with AI networking +40% y/y as key driver).
